- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 2–5%.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (e.g., <90% of avg), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–5 days; if sentiment is bullish, anticipate 1–2 day lead; if bearish, expect 1–2 day lag.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment shift.
